summary: We have created a 3D mission-based training game. It is accessible and easy to understand for various age groups, ranging from 7 to 18+. Developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge, our project addresses the junior astronaut training challenge by turning complex space concepts into an interactive, engaging learning experience. It is important because it bridges education and inspiration, helping players develop essential problem-solving skills while fostering a lifelong passion for space exploration.
details:
We developed an interactive, web-based 3D mission training game designed to educate junior astronauts and space enthusiasts of all ages. Built natively in Unity using C#, Blender, Java Script and accelerated by Claude Code for efficient development, the application delivers a lightweight, seamless browser experience without sacrificing high-end simulation quality.

How It Works & Key Features

  • Web-Accessible & Lightweight: Optimized for instant browser play, ensuring zero friction for users to jump straight into training.
  • Official NASA Data: All in-game information, mission parameters, and environmental data are strictly validated and sourced directly from official NASA repositories.
  • Realistic Physics Engine: The game accurately simulates real-world physical laws and space mechanics, providing an authentic foundation for astronaut training.
  • Mission-Based Learning: Players tackle structured challenges that test their problem-solving skills, resource management, and understanding of space environments.

Technical Stack & Innovation

  • Engine & Language: Unity (WebGL build) & C#.
  • Development Workflow: Streamlined and optimized using Claude Code to accelerate scripting, physics tuning, and UI logic.
  • Data Integrity: Seamlessly integrates real space datasets into interactive 3D mechanics.

Impact & Creativity

The project bridges education and interactive entertainment by turning complex aerospace concepts into an intuitive, gamified experience. By making astronaut training accessible directly through a web browser, it inspires the next generation of space explorers, students, and science enthusiasts globally.
